hints: Remember that an addition polymer is made by opening the C=C double bond of an alkene monomer, so work backwards from single bonds to a double bond.
Look at the two-carbon repeating pattern in the chain, each -CH2-CHCl- unit contains one carbon with Cl and one without.
Add a double bond back between those two carbons to rebuild the small alkene that must have joined together to make this chain.
walkthrough:
**Recall how addition polymers form**

Think of polymerisation in reverse. Monomer alkenes open their $C=C$ to form new $C-C$ single bonds in a long chain.

$$ \text{monomer } C=C \rightarrow \text{polymer } -C-C- $$

**Spot the repeat unit in the section**

The section shown is $-CHCl-CH_2-CH_2-CHCl-$. If you slide the window a little, this is just two identical units joined head to tail.

$$ -\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}- $$

**Rebuild the monomer**

Take one repeat unit, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-$, and put the double bond back in. That gives $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$, chloroethene.

$$ -\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}- \leftarrow \text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl} $$

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Cl}$ has three carbons with Cl on the end carbon. Its polymer would have a $-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ side chain, not Cl directly on the backbone as shown.
options.B: Correct. $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$ (chloroethene) opens its double bond to give the repeat unit $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-$. Two of these joined give exactly the $-\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-$ section shown.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHCHCl}$ is a three-carbon unit and would introduce $\text{CH}_3$ groups into the backbone. The polymer section has only two-carbon units with no methyl branches.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CHClCHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ is a four-carbon molecule with two Cl atoms. An addition monomer for this chain must be a two-carbon alkene, not a long dichloro unit.
